The B-24... That was a heavy bomber known as the Liberator and was made by Consolidated Aircraft, a now defunct company that used to be HQed in San Diego. It used something called a "Davis" wing, which allowed it to cruise faster and higher, while allowing it to carry heavier loads.

It was not just used by the US Army Air Corps. The UK's Royal Air Force made good use of it. What's notable is that the RAF used it regularly to completely cross the Atlantic ocean, as it had the range to do so. It was the first model of airplane that was regularly used to make that journey.

There was also a cargo version, the C-87. That had an even longer range. There was a PB4Y-2 that was based on the same fuselage and used through the Korean War by the USN and sometime (I forget how long - but ending before 1960) afterwards by the USCG. That version was known as "Privateer."
